checkedAlternates.risk: Zoos have gift shops and are ticketed, which brings them near "buy something".
checkedAlternates.resolution: You go to a zoo to spend time outdoors; the shop is incidental, and the shopping row is four unambiguous shops.

checkedAlternates.risk: Train stations serve long-distance travel, which is what the airport is for.
checkedAlternates.resolution: The split is air travel versus local ground transport. If blind testers read the station as long-distance, relabel the group as "to catch a train or bus" rather than moving the item.

checkedAlternates.risk: Playgrounds sit inside shopping centres in many cities.
checkedAlternates.resolution: The standalone reading is an outdoor play area, which is what the group means.

checkedAlternates.risk: Bakeries with seating read as a place to spend time.
checkedAlternates.resolution: A bakery is a shop; the outdoor row is deliberately three open-air places.

authorReview.notes: The single-item row is the airport, which is the only place in the set you visit to leave the city entirely.

blindPlaytest.notes: Watch the train station. It is the only item where the rival reading has a real argument behind it.
